historicalContract: Lesson identities, heading IDs/text/order, quiz module identifiers, question counts and answer indices remain unchanged. Options match the baseline plus the explicit reviewed factual corrections in qa/quiz-contract-amendments.json. Question and explanation prose may be intentionally edited.

beforeOptions: Chinese plants use the FBR silane route, which cannot reach better than 6N purity

Electronic grade requires 10-100x lower boron and phosphorus, etched and cleanroom-handled chunk, FZ test-ingot verification and 1-2 year customer qualification, and the whole EG market is only ~40-50 kt/yr, so incumbents with long-term contracts and traceable supply chains keep it
US export controls prohibit the import of any Chinese polysilicon for semiconductor use
Chinese polysilicon is sold only as granules, which cannot be loaded into a Czochralski crucible
afterOptions: FBR chemistry cannot produce semiconductor-purity silicon, regardless of process control
Electronic-grade supply needs stringent impurity and surface-cleanliness control, verification and customer qualification; solar tonnage alone does not demonstrate those requirements
Every semiconductor customer requires its polysilicon to be manufactured in the same country as its wafer factory
Granular silicon cannot be loaded into a Czochralski crucible
reviewedQuizAmendments.reason: Replace an unsupported incumbent-only and nationality-specific premise with product purity, consistency and customer qualification.

beforeOptions: China cannot obtain 300 mm silicon wafers of sufficient purity
SMIC lacks EDA tools capable of place-and-route below 7 nm

Without EUV, each shrink requires more DUV multi-patterning passes, so mask count, cost, and defect exposure rise while yield falls (reported well below 50% at 5 nm-class), making the node possible but uneconomic and 3 nm-class not credible
SMIC's fabs are limited to 200 mm wafers
afterOptions: The foundry cannot obtain silicon wafers pure enough for advanced logic
Every transistor must use a different EDA tool because the exposure wavelength changed

Additional patterning and alignment steps can increase cost, cycle time and defect exposure; a teardown can establish dimensions and structures, but does not establish factory yield or cost per good die
The foundry must switch from 300 mm to 200 mm wafers to use additional exposures
reviewedQuizAmendments.reason: Remove unsupported process-node, yield and profitability assertions; test multi-patterning tradeoffs and the evidence limits of chip teardowns.

beforeOptions: About 50% of both; a major earthquake near Tainan
About 90% of both; a naval blockade that stops inbound chemicals, gases and spares and outbound wafers within weeks
About 70% of wafers and 30% of packaging; a US export-control action against TSMC
About 90% of wafers but under 20% of packaging; a typhoon season power outage
afterOptions: Factories can use any locally available chemicals without qualification, so only damaged equipment stops production
An interruption to qualified chemicals, gases, spare parts or transport can stop output; alternative foundries and packaging technologies require product-specific redesign and qualification
A foundry's headquarters determines where every wafer and package it sells is physically manufactured
All advanced packaging is the same as CoWoS, so another OSAT can take over the process immediately
reviewedQuizAmendments.reason: Distinguish TSMC-specific CoWoS supply risk from the broader advanced-packaging market and preserve product qualification requirements.
